name: Inspirit AI Scholars (Live Online)
deadline: Nov 30, 2026 (Winter 2026 cohort, rolling admissions)
eligibility: Grades 9-12 or equivalent; no coding experience needed. Egypt/international: online program, nationality limits Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only. 10 sessions, 25 hours.
funding: Paid: USD $1,400 (official page). Financial aid: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: fast, structured AI/Python intro with a mentor-led project; fits a coder. Cons: costs money, no travel, mostly a paid course, not a competition. Admission is easy compared with the others on this list. The deadline is 5 days away.

name: Hack Club Expedition (YSWS)
deadline: Rolling. Galway hackathon Dec 4-6, 2026; Bergen (Norway) April 2027 needs 100 logged hours. Exact cutoffs: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Teens 13-18, free to join, no application. Egypt eligible by the page wording; visa support: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Hybrid. Build online, then optional in-person trips (Galway, Ireland, 4-6 Dec; Bergen, Norway, April 2027, 40 teens).
funding: Free. Hours unlock gear grants or travel grants. Exact travel coverage per trip: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: you build real projects, it rewards time spent, and it has real trips. Cons: Schengen/Irish visas for an Egyptian passport are the main risk, and Galway is only 9 days away. The Bergen spot needs 100 hours. Easy to enter, competitive for trip seats.

name: Polygence Research Program
deadline: Dec 15, 2026, 11:59pm PT (priority deadline); later deadlines follow
eligibility: Middle and high school students; a 15-year-old in grade 9 fits. International students accepted: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only. Ten sessions with a PhD mentor over 3-6 months; you can pick a CS or logic/philosophy project.
funding: Paid: programs start around $3,000 (official FAQ). A fully funded Research for Impact Scholarship exists; terms: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: you get a real CS or philosophy research project with a mentor, and the output looks good on applications. Cons: expensive without the scholarship, and there is no travel. The scholarship is competitive and needs a personal-impact story.

name: Lumiere Research Scholar Program
deadline: Reported Dec 27, 2026 by a third-party listing only. Official deadline: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Grades 9-12 reported by third parties; official page lists financial aid and scholarships. Egypt eligibility: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only. About 12 weeks, one-on-one with a PhD mentor.
funding: Paid. Third parties report about $3,390; the official page offers financial aid and scholarships. Price: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: a paper in CS or philosophy with mentor feedback, and financial aid is offered. Cons: the price and deadline are not confirmed on the official page, there is no travel, and it is selective with an interview round.

name: Coolest Projects Online 2027
deadline: Entries open Jan 13, 2027. Closing date: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page. Livestream Jun 23, 2027
eligibility: Any young person up to 18, anywhere. Ages 13+ can register their own project; teams up to 5.
travelDuration: Remote only.
funding: Free. Certificates and feedback for all entrants; VIP judges highlight some projects.
fit: Pros: free, global, any code project, and your age is fine. Cons: it is a showcase, so there are no big prizes and no travel. Good for getting a project in front of people.

name: Global Game Jam 2027
deadline: Jammer sign-ups open Dec 1, 2026; jam Jan 25-31, 2027 (sites choose 48 hours)
eligibility: Open to all; under-18 rules depend on the local jam site. Cairo-area sites: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In-person at a local site or online. No international travel.
funding: Typically free. Local site fees: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: 48 hours to build a game with a team, free, low barrier, good first hackathon. Cons: no international travel and no cash prizes. Look for a Cairo or Mansoura site, or join online.

name: Hack Club Crossroads
deadline: Event Feb 2027. Qualification is by building projects; cutoff Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Teens 13-18 (both ends included). Open source software projects. Egypt eligibility: no country limit stated; visa: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person: 65 hours of building, then 5 days by train through Berlin, Paris, Brussels and Milan with 30 teens.
funding: Free for those who qualify: train passes, food and accommodation. International flights to Berlin: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: it is a rare free Europe trip built for coders, and it matches your wish for travel plus programming. Cons: only 30 seats, a Schengen visa is not guaranteed (the organisers only promise to help), and flights are unconfirmed. Begin logging project hours now.

name: Wolfram High School Summer Research Program
deadline: Early Decision / Regular Decision rounds (deposit dates Feb 26 and Apr 30, 2027). Application deadlines: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Ages 14-17; cannot turn 18 during the program. International students accepted and must arrange visas.
travelDuration: In person at Bentley University near Boston, USA, June 28 - July 17, 2027 (3 weeks).
funding: Paid: $6,500 including room and board and a $500 non-refundable deposit. Financial aid: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: three weeks in the USA, a project with Wolfram staff, and strong computing focus. Cons: a US visa is a real hurdle and the fee is high with no confirmed aid. Realistic only with funding.

name: Rise (Schmidt Futures and Rhodes Trust)
deadline: 2027 cycle deadline not posted: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Ages 15-17 as of July 1 of the cohort year (from a third-party summary); no citizenship restriction. You turn 15 in 2026 and 16 in Sept 2027, so the 2027 cohort fits.
travelDuration: Mostly remote. In-person events: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
funding: Free. Support may include need-based scholarships, mentorship and further funding.
fit: Pros: a lifelong network and a global talent search, free. Cons: the focus is service to others, so you need a project that helps people, and only up to 100 fellows are chosen worldwide. Very competitive.

name: picoCTF / CyLab Security Academy
deadline: 2027 dates not posted. The 2026 event ran Mar 9-19 (registration Feb 1 - Mar 17). 2027: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Participants 13+; middle school, high school and college students; worldwide. Cash prize eligibility depends on residence: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only.
funding: Free to play. Prize eligibility for non-US students: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: free, strong for logic and security skills, and you can practise year-round on the platform. Cons: no travel, and prize rules may exclude non-US residents. Start practising now.

name: International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI) 2027
deadline: Registration reported open (Nov 2026). National selection dates for Egypt: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: High school students on national teams. Age cap and Egypt's national selection process: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person in Singapore, July 4-10, 2027.
funding: Host-country coverage terms: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: top-tier AI contest, a trip to Singapore, and strong fit. Cons: you need to be picked through a national process, which is not confirmed for Egypt. Ask your school and the Egyptian ministry.

name: International Philosophy Olympiad (IPO) 2027
deadline: National rounds before May 2027. Egypt's selection: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Secondary students on national delegations. Egypt participation: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person. An Austrian organiser page reports Astana, May 13-16, 2027 (host city: verify on the official page).
funding: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: fits your logic and philosophy interest. Cons: I could not confirm that Egypt sends a team, so this may be unreachable. Check the IPO site for an Egyptian contact before investing time.

name: International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) 2027 via EOI
deadline: Egyptian Olympiad in Informatics (EOI) rounds; 2027 dates Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: High school students. Egypt selects its team through the EOI at AASTMT's Regional Informatics Center (https://www.eoi-eg.org/).
travelDuration: In person at Hasso Plattner Institute, Potsdam, Germany, Sept 12-19, 2027.
funding: Team costs are usually covered by the national organisers: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: the most prestigious programming contest, and it fits your coding focus. Cons: very competitive, needs strong algorithms, and a Schengen visa is needed. At 15 you can start early since the team forms over several years. Join EOI training and Codeforces now.

name: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize
deadline: 2026 cycle is closed. 2027 dates: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page (the 2026 deadline was reported as May 31)
eligibility: Any nationality, under 19; Junior category for under 15 on the deadline. No minimum age. Parental consent is needed for under-18 interviews.
travelDuration: Remote essay. Winners may be invited to events: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
funding: Free to enter per official page text. Reported prize: $5,000 scholarship for first place per category; check the official page.
fit: Pros: Philosophy and Science and Technology categories, free, and no age minimum. Cons: no guaranteed travel, and the judges are very selective. A strong essay in Philosophy is a realistic goal.

name: World Robot Olympiad (WRO) via Egypt national rounds
deadline: Egypt regional and national rounds ran Aug-Sep in past years. 2027 registration: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Ages 8-19 by category; Future Engineers (self-driving cars) is 14-22 per the 2026 rules. You enter through an Egyptian team and national organiser.
travelDuration: Hybrid. National finals in Egypt; the 2026 international final is Dec 8-10 in Puerto Rico. 2027 venue: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
funding: Team registration fees apply. One 2024 Egyptian listing showed LE 5,500; current fee Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: Future Engineers is a good programming and engineering fit, and it can lead to a trip abroad. Cons: you need a team, a coach and the fees. Qualifying slots are limited, and visas can be tricky.

name: FIRST Global Challenge (Team Egypt)
deadline: Team selection by the Egyptian partner. 2027 timeline: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Students aged 14-18. One national team per country, chosen by FIRST Global's in-country partner.
travelDuration: In person abroad. The 2026 event was Oct 7-10 in Incheon, Korea. 2027 host: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
funding: Team travel is normally handled by the national team organiser. Costs to students: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: a real international trip and a team-engineering challenge. Cons: only one national team, selected by a partner, so odds are low and the process is opaque. Contact the Egyptian partner via the Team Egypt page.

name: Emergent Ventures Grant
deadline: Rolling
eligibility: Applicants must be 13+. All parts of the world welcome. Proposal up to 1,500 words.
travelDuration: Remote.
funding: Free to apply. Grant sizes are project-specific, and there is no typical amount.
fit: Pros: age fits, global, funds an unusual idea such as a software tool. Cons: no travel, and you need a concrete project plan. Realistically competitive.

name: Erasmus+ Youth Exchanges
deadline: Rolling; depends on each sending organisation and project
eligibility: Ages 13-30 (group leader 18+). Joins through a sending organisation or youth group, not individually. Egypt can take part in projects with an EU organiser (per third-party summary): Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person in Europe, 5-21 days.
funding: Project grants usually cover travel, accommodation and meals (third-party summary; confirm per project).
fit: Pros: a real, funded trip to Europe at your age. Cons: you need a youth organisation to send you, themes are non-tech (often social topics), and visas apply. You must avoid environmental-themed exchanges.

name: Rotary Youth Exchange
deadline: Set by your local Rotary club and district: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Students ages 15-19. You apply through a Rotary club in Egypt.
travelDuration: In person abroad: long-term (a school year) or short-term (weeks).
funding: Costs vary by district: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: a true cultural exchange; your age is right at the start of the range. Cons: not tech-focused, costs and placement vary, and it needs a local club. Ask a Rotary club in Mansoura or Cairo.

name: Sakura Science High School Program (Japan, JST)
deadline: Selected through partner institutions; application path Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: High school students invited from selected countries. A 2025 group included 56 students from Egypt, Ghana, India, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Zambia. How individuals are chosen: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person, one week in Japan (visits to labs and JAXA/RIKEN type institutions).
funding: Invitation program run by JST. Coverage: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: Egypt was in the 2025 group and Japan is a strong tech destination. Cons: you cannot apply directly as far as I could confirm, and it is a science tour, not a competition. Ask your school.

name: ISEF Egypt (ASTF) to Regeneron ISEF
deadline: Egyptian fair timeline: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Students aged 14-18 (grades 9-12), all school types in Egypt. Winners can go to the international ISEF.
travelDuration: In person. The international ISEF is abroad. Host city: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
funding: Prizes and scholarships at ISEF (official page claims up to $4 million in total). Travel cover for Egyptian winners: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: computer science projects compete here, and Egyptian students can qualify, with a real trip for winners. Cons: you need a solid original project, and categories lean to lab science. Many projects are environment-themed, so avoid those.

name: TEKNOFEST Technology Competitions
deadline: Applications open online per competition: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Each competition has its own age, team and country rules; some are open to school students. Egypt-specific rules: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: In person in Turkey for finals.
funding: Prizes exist; travel costs for foreign teams: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: big prizes and a festival abroad, with AI, robotics and software categories. Cons: many categories are for older teams or Turkish institutions, and I could not confirm what is open to a 15-year-old Egyptian. Read each competition's rules.

name: The Knowledge Society (TKS)
deadline: Rolling cohorts: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Ages 13-17, 80+ countries.
travelDuration: Remote (virtual program) or in-person in some cities (e.g. Dubai).
funding: Paid. Virtual: $489 per month plus a $1,000 deposit (USD) per the official page; in-person is higher. Aid: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: a 10-month builder community, a good fit for ambitious teens. Cons: expensive over ten months, with no travel in the virtual version. Check the aid options.

name: Qiskit Global Summer School
deadline: 2027 dates Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page (the 2026 school ran Jul 13-24 with a Jun 19 registration deadline)
eligibility: Open to students, educators, developers and professionals; Python familiarity is recommended. Age limit for minors: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only, two weeks.
funding: Free in 2026 per the listing; 2027: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
fit: Pros: free, a hard and unusual topic, and good for logic-minded coders. Cons: no travel, and it is easy to get lost without strong math. Do it for the skill.

name: Stanford Code in Place
deadline: 2026 class started April 2026; 2027 dates Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page
eligibility: Learners with no programming experience; online worldwide. Age rules: Unconfirmed / Verify on Official Page.
travelDuration: Remote only.
funding: Free, with a certificate.
fit: Pros: free, Stanford CS106A Python content. Cons: for beginners, so probably below your level if you already code. Useful only as a refresher or a teaching experience.
